2013_045_020513mtg.paragraph: Agenda, minutes and supporting exhibits for the Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting held at 7:00 PM on February 5, 2013 in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy. The consent agenda carried four sets of January 2013 minutes plus the December 2012 Treasurer's Report, which reported total disbursements in period of $4,731,168.92. Business items authorized preparation of an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds for a November 2013 school improvement bond issue, adopted a 2012-2013 budget amendment showing amended General Fund expenditures of $131,488,075, and awarded a web filtering bid to Phantom Technologies for $44,768.00.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, 7:00 PM, February 5, 2013, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
Minutes of the January 15, 2013 special meeting (closed session on negotiations under the Open Meetings Act, PA 267, Section 8(c), resolution 13-001, carried 6-0 with Hauff absent), the January 15 organizational meeting, the January 15 regular meeting, the January 22 workshop, and the December 2012 Treasurer's Report. Organizational resolutions 13-002 through 13-010 passed Yes 7, No 0: Nancy Philippart president and Todd Miletti vice president through December 31, 2013; Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for January through December 2013; depository and investment resolution naming Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase, Citizen's Bank, Comerica, Fifth Third, MILAF, PFM Securities and PNC, with investments governed by Board Policy D-1103; Judy Holmes designated to post meeting notices.

**December 2012 Treasurer's Report** (memo from Mark S. Rajter dated January 30, 2013)

| Item | Amount |

| Total - General Fund (101/120/122) | $2,258,227.86 |
| Total - Special Revenue Funds | $89,992.03 |
| Total - Other Funds | $152,902.94 |
| Total check disbursements | $2,501,122.83 |
| ACH debits | $26,647.21 |
| Outgoing wire transfers | $1,977,897.00 |
| P-Card purchases | $233,074.49 |
| Prior period void disbursements | ($7,572.61) |
| **Total disbursements in period** | **$4,731,168.92** |

The attached Pentamation check register (report ACCTPA21, run 01/15/2013, accounting period 7/13) totals $2,501,122.83. Largest checks include MESSA premiums and COBRA $908,296.40, Enviro Clean Services custodial contract $249,100.56, Blue Cross Blue Shield January premiums $151,344.12, First Group America transportation $113,849.73 (General Fund) and $107,235.49 (Special Ed), and Oakland County Treasurer $96,822.97. December YTD budget reports show General Fund revenue of $45,108,963 actual against a $129,234,265 adopted budget and expenditures of $50,205,694 actual against $132,398,263.

**Personnel**
Probationary contracts for Zachary MacIntosh (1.0 FTE Social Studies, Baker Middle School), Letitia Mason (.5 GSRP, Hill Elementary), Megan Sulewski (1.0 FTE French, Athens High School) and Leah Vohs (.5 ESL Resource, Schroeder Elementary). Mark Washington recommended as Director of Technology on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure beginning February 11, 2013.

**Curriculum**
Enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Frederick R. Ignatovich, Stanfred Consultants: district enrollment ran 12,182 in 2007/2008 to 12,391 (unofficial count) in 2012/2013, with projected totals of 12,440 for 2013/2014 rising to 12,662 for 2017/2018 including ECP, SCSE and GROW students. Athens and Troy High remain closed to open enrollment for 2013/2014 except not more than 25 ninth grade students from the Troy High attendance area, applications February 6-22, 2013.

**Business**
Authorization to prepare an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds under the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program for a November 2013 election; the Exhibit A ballot leaves dollar and millage figures blank and caps the term at not more than fifteen (15) years. The 2012-2013 budget amendment appropriates $131,488,075 (General Fund), $8,805,399 (Special Revenue), $18,113,148 (Debt Service), $290,713 (Capital Projects) and $25,000 (Internal Service). A web filtering bid was awarded to Phantom Technologies for $44,768.00 (iBoss 14500, three-year subscription for 5,000 nodes) through Oakland Schools cooperative pricing.

**Other**
Second reading and consideration of revisions to Board Policy K-1303, Commercial Advertising, first read January 15, 2013.
2013_045_020513mtg.verbose:
The Troy School District Board of Education, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us), convened its regular meeting at 7:00 PM on February 5, 2013 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools; public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per person. The consent agenda carried minutes of the January 15, 2013 special, organizational and regular meetings, the January 22, 2013 workshop, and the December 2012 Treasurer's Report.

JANUARY 15 SPECIAL MEETING. Called to order by President Philippart at 5:34 p.m.; present Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood, absent Mr. Hauff, with Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt. Resolution 13-001 (Fleming/Edmunds), citing the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), carried 6-0 to enter closed session on negotiations at 5:36 p.m.; adjourned 6:50 p.m., submitted by Todd Miletti, Secretary.

JANUARY 15 ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING. Called to order 7:00 p.m., all seven members present, approximately 65 in the audience; adjourned 7:12 p.m. Resolutions 13-002 through 13-010 each passed Yes 7, No 0: Philippart acting chairperson; Judy Holmes temporary secretary; Ms. Philippart president and Mr. Miletti vice president until December 31, 2013; the secretary election under 13-005 (sidebar labeled Fleming, motion text as printed naming Miletti); Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for January through December 2013; fund depositories and investments; the Superintendent designated Deputy Secretary for 2013; Judy Holmes, Secretary to the Superintendent of Schools, designated to post notices; and the 2013 meeting calendar adopted. The depository resolution names Bank of America, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Citizen's Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), PFM Securities, Inc. and PNC Bank. Checks carry Rajter's facsimile signature, with emergency handwritten signature by Rajter or Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler; Bank of America health care claim checks over $10,000 need the added signature of Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources, or Monica Papasian, Finance Director; the Comerica flexible spending account is paid by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc. Investments follow Board Policy D-1103 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code. Certified by Todd Miletti, January 15, 2013.

JANUARY 15 REGULAR MEETING. Called to order 7:13 p.m., all seven present, about 60 in the audience; adjourned 8:26 p.m., submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary. Fall senior scholar athletes with a 3.5 cumulative grade point average were recognized, along with all-state athletes Zachary Doepke, Brett Forman, Mitch Guitar, Nicole Hahn, Max Klitzke and Jennifer Yang. Actions: 13-011 consent agenda; 13-012 new hires Renee Boogren and Nichelle Dowgiert; 13-013 and 13-016 Schools of Choice under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, each for 100 nonresident kindergarten and 30 nonresident first-grade students in 2013-2014; 13-014 UPS replacement at Morse Elementary to J. B. Electrical Company, $28,115.00; 13-015 purchase of 22 multi-function copiers from Konica Minolta, $250,796.00, with a five-year service agreement estimated at an additional $44,250 per year; 13-017 and 13-018 Schools of Choice for 25 non-resident students each in grades 6-8 at Baker Middle School. Dr. Fowler's goals update covered college/career readiness, subgroup interventions, preparation for the November 2013 bond election, and a data processing review due by June 2013; a post-Sandy Hook security update described work with the Troy Police, added entry-point security systems, and "How to Respond to an Active Shooter" training through Homeland Security at Oakland Schools. The January 22 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 9:04 p.m. on the 2012/2013 First Appropriation Act, the 2013/14-2015/16 budget forecast, a bond issue survey, and bond ballot language.

TREASURER'S REPORT, DECEMBER 2012 (memo from Mark S. Rajter, January 30, 2013, 248-823-4022). Check disbursements by fund: General Fund (101) $2,087,120.41; Grant Fund (120) $327.14; Special Education (122) $170,780.31; Food Service (520) $17,056.54; Troy Career Center (529) $54,932.61; Community Education (530) $18,002.88; Debt Funds (304, 306, 307) $25,274.06; Student Activity (700, 701) $127,028.88; Memorial Scholarship (750) $600.00. Wires included MPSERS PD/MIP/TDP $892,527.00 and MPSERS DB $894,567.18, payroll transfers of $1,717,362.00 and $1,730,818.95, a $4,000,000.00 year-end payroll and A/P transfer, the Sodexo October 2012 invoice of $406,632.70, and a severance VRIP payment of $84,336.49. DECEMBER YTD BUDGET REPORTS. General Fund (101, 120, 122, 140) revenue: adopted $129,234,265, actual $45,108,963, uncollected $84,125,302 (65.10%). Expenditures: adopted $132,398,263, actual $50,205,694, encumbered $60,184,143, available $22,008,426 (16.62%), with total instruction budgeted $89,513,753 and total support services $42,698,715. Excess revenue over expenditures ($3,163,998); fund balance $20,591,023 at July 1, 2012 and $17,427,025 at June 30, 2013. Consolidated special revenue: revenue $9,094,808 budget/$3,337,197 actual; expenditures $9,306,329 budget/$3,015,321 actual; fund balance $2,185,989 to $1,974,468. Food Service (520) revenue $3,414,309 against expenditures of $3,537,041 with salaries at zero; Troy Career Center (529) fully federally funded at $3,210,292 with a June 30, 2013 balance of $270; Facilities Rental (535) collected nothing against $181,740. Debt service: property taxes $17,174,042 budgeted and $9,105,006 collected, redemption of principal $13,055,000, interest on debt $5,179,000, fund balance $(1,825,694) to $(3,129,052). Capital Projects (404) capital outlay actual $694,010 against a $185,000 budget; Capital Projects Maintenance (499) $40,153; Internal Service ERI (681) $116,000 of VRIP expense.

CHECK REGISTER. Pentamation Enterprises report ACCTPA21, "Check Register - By Fund," dated 01/15/2013, criteria gl_cash between A1001 and A1005 and ck_date between 12/01/2012 and 12/31/2012, accounting period 7/13, total report $2,501,122.83. Notable payments: MESSA premium and COBRA $908,296.40; Enviro Clean Services $249,100.56 plus $4,190.66 of event cleanups; Blue Cross Blue Shield January premiums $151,344.12; First Group America $113,849.73 (General Fund) and $107,235.49 (Special Ed); Oakland County Treasurer $96,822.97; Houghton Mifflin/McDougal $46,498.85; Integrys Energy Services $43,284.22; R K A Petroleum $37,899.36; City of Troy water $32,017.09 and truck service $18,529.40; Oakland Community College $30,250.00; Arch Environmental $22,541.87; Clark Hill PLC $21,725.90 and $17,592.77; Crossroads Church donation to AHS student council $17,430.00; MHSAA football semifinal $16,569.60; K12 Virtual School $13,906.00; Executive Energy Services $10,800.00. Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood each received a $50.00 board payment under object 1140. Fund totals include 122 $170,780.31, 304 $19,169.23, 306 $6,104.83, 700 $126,656.84, 701 $372.04 and 750 $600.00.

PERSONNEL. Item 6.A recommends probationary contracts for the remainder of 2012-2013: Zachary MacIntosh, 1.0 FTE Social Studies, Baker Middle School (B.A. Oakland University April 2012); Letitia Mason, .5 Great Start Readiness Program, Hill Elementary (B.A. Clark Atlanta University 1995, M.A. Wayne State University 1997, Troy resident); Megan Sulewski, 1.0 FTE French, Athens High School (B.S. Central Michigan University December 2012); Leah Vohs, .5 ESL Resource Teacher, Schroeder Elementary (B.A. Wayne State University 2000, M.A. 2002). Item 6.B recommends Mr. Mark Washington as Director of Technology on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure beginning February 11, 2013; 18 years as a Director of Technology at Port Huron Area School District, Wayland Union Schools and Marysville Schools, 22 years total in public school technology, B.S. in Technical Communications from Western Michigan University.

CURRICULUM. Item 7.A, enrollment projections by Dr. Frederick R. Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants using Michigan Department of Community Health and National Center for Health Statistics birth data. Enrollment history: 12,182 (2007/2008), 12,165 (2008/2009), 12,069 (2009/2010), 12,056 (2010/2011), 12,328 (2011/2012), 12,391 unofficial (2012/2013). The birth-to-kindergarten ratio moved from 4.69 in 96-97 to 5.93 in 12-13. Non-residents attending Troy grew from 295 in Fall 2002 to 694 in Fall 2012, while residents attending other public districts went from 299 in Fall 2002 to 454 in Fall 2011. Fall 2012 schools-of-choice intake: kindergarten 103, first grade 24, middle school 25 at Baker only, International Academy-East freshmen 53. Projected enrollment including ECP, SCSE and GROW: 12,440 (2013/2014), 12,571 (2014/2015), 12,612 (2015/2016), 12,608 (2016/2017), 12,662 (2017/2018). Item 7.B closes Athens and Troy High to open enrollment for 2013/2014 except not more than 25 ninth grade students residing in the Troy High attendance area, applications February 6-22, 2013, with siblings of Athens students in grades 9-11 allowed to open enroll.

BUSINESS. Item 8.A authorizes preparation of an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds for a School Improvement Bond issue on the November 2013 ballot under the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, with the Superintendent authorized to select the architect, bond counsel, construction manager, technology designer and financial advisor. Exhibit A, the official ballot for the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, leaves borrowing amount and millage blank, covers technology equipment, remodeling, school buses, additions and site improvements, is guaranteed under Section 16 of Article IX of the State Constitution of 1963, and may be outstanding not more than fifteen (15) years. Certified by Paula Fleming, Secretary, under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

Item 8.B, the 2012-2013 budget amendment resolution, appropriates $131,488,075 (General Fund), $8,805,399 (Special Revenue), $18,113,148 (Debt Service), $290,713 (Capital Projects) and $25,000 (Internal Service). Amended General Fund revenues: local $37,213,220, state $80,549,791, federal $3,820,728, transfers $8,909,863, total $130,493,602; beginning fund balance restated to $23,078,581 and total available to appropriate $153,572,183. Amended expenditures: total instruction $87,184,807, total support services $43,040,924, community services $132,663, outgoing transfers $1,129,681; excess revenues over expenditures ($994,473); ending fund balance June 30, 2013 $22,084,108. Revenue mix local 28.52%, state 61.72%, federal 2.93%, transfers 6.83%; expenditure mix instruction 66.31%, support services 32.73%, community services 0.10%, transfers and other 0.86%. Debt funds show a levy amended to $17,156,740, interest on debt $4,513,921 and an ending balance of ($2,666,557). The resolution text prints $131,941,046 for the General Fund and $18,133,148 for Debt Service, differing from the expenditure totals shown elsewhere in the same item.

Item 8.C awards the web filtering bid to Phantom Technologies for $44,768.00 from the 2012-2013 General Fund. A January 31, 2013 memorandum from Ken Crawford, Interim Acting Director of Technology, Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois (248/823-5090), to Dr. Barbara Fowler notes Merri Lynn Colligan began research in Fall 2012 to replace Deep Nines, that Barracuda and Phantom products were each tested 30 days, and that the iBoss 14500 costs $6,964 more than the Barracuda 810 over the three-year subscription while adding a redundant filter, redundant power supplies, better reporting and granular YouTube EDU control. Quote Qt21513 dated 11 Jan 2013 from Phantom Technologies, Inc., 9950 Summers Ridge Rd., Building 160, San Diego, California 92121, lists the iBoss Enterprise 14500 at $3,995.00, a three-year subscription for 5,000 nodes at $35,988.00 and two copper bypass interfaces at $790.00, subtotal $44,768.00 under Oakland Schools RFP pricing. Bidder ranking: MBM $37,803.84 (Barracuda), Teoma $44,711.25 (Barracuda), Oakland Schools co-op $44,768.00 (iBoss), BorderLan $54,635.00 (iBoss), Phantom $59,779.85 (iBoss).

OTHER. Item 10.A is the second reading of revisions to Board Policy K-1303, Commercial Advertising, within Section K-1300, Advertising and Distribution of Materials in the Schools. The policy bars commercial material causing substantial and material interference with normal school activities from district-owned property without written consent of the superintendent or designee, permits display on personal vehicles parked on school property, and restricts personnel from using district resources, technology, District e-mail and student or parent contact information for commercial purposes. Adopted May 3, 1976; revised January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998, April 20, 2010 and June 19, 2012.
